subject: Staged POC credits + volume discount proposal for BrightLabs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@brightlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged POC credits + volume discount proposal for BrightLabs

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Per our call, BrightLabs is planning a 3-week POC to validate semantic search + recommendations (approx. 750k–1.2M tokens estimated). You asked for a simple, low-risk commercial structure that gives you visibility into unit economics and optional scale discounts if you commit to a retention/launch plan.

Quick proposal from our side (high level):
- Pilot window: 3 weeks, billed usage-but-with-credit-offset.
- One-time launch credit: $12,000 (applied as token credit over the pilot).
- Commit tiers (post-pilot, 12-month):
  * Tier A: commit $50k (est. 40M tokens/mo) — 12% per-token discount
  * Tier B: commit $100k (est. 90M tokens/mo) — 18% per-token discount + priority scheduling
  * Tier C: commit $250k (est. 250M tokens/mo) — 26% per-token discount + reserved capacity add-on
- Credit release mechanics: 50% of pilot credit up front, 25% on completion of ingestion milestone, 25% upon first month invoice after commit. Credits are forfeitable if customer cancels within 30 days of commit.

I attached a short term sheet (redwood_poc_credit_sheet.pdf) that maps the credit mechanics to a simple billing example based on your estimated token usage. Pricing here is for our hosted API (usage-based); we can provide Dedicated pricing if you need reserved GPUs.

If this direction looks reasonable I suggest a 30-minute follow-up with procurement to align on cancellation windows and SOW timing. Marissa/Karthik — tagging you for any constraints on approvals or if we should escalate to RevOps for a one-off launch incentive.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Exec, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood_poc_credit_sheet.pdf (proposal, 34KB), redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf (terms, 18KB)

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@brightlabs.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@brightlabs.ai, BrightLabs Legal <legal@brightlabs.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged POC credits + volume discount proposal for BrightLabs

Hi Connor —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and our engineering lead before we sync: 
1) Can you confirm the effective per-token price after the stated discounts for Tier A/B/C (we need a dollar-per-1k-token figure)?
2) For the pilot credits: if we scale beyond the 1.2M token estimate, will overage be billed at list price with credits applied, or prorated?
3) What does the cancellation / clawback process look like in practice (procurement asks for simple language we can review with legal)?

Our ideal timeline: start ingestion next Monday (4/19), run the 3-week test, and have a commercial decision by May 10. 

If you could provide a numeric example and a one-page summary procurement can share with legal, that will help. Can you also confirm whether the credits show up as invoice line items (we prefer visibility over statement-level adjustments).

Thanks — looping in procure@brightlabs.ai for availability.

—Elena
Elena Rodriguez
Head of AI Platforms, BrightLabs
elena@brightlabs.ai

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged POC credits + volume discount proposal for BrightLabs

Hi Elena — thanks for the great questions. Short answers and a worked example below.

1) Effective per-token price (USD per 1k tokens) after discount (example base list price = $0.60 / 1k tokens):
  - Tier A (12% off): $0.528 / 1k
  - Tier B (18% off): $0.492 / 1k
  - Tier C (26% off): $0.444 / 1k

2) Pilot overage behavior: overage during the pilot is billed at list price and credits are applied to the invoice in the same billing period (i.e., credits are line-item offsets shown on the invoice). We can cap pilot overages to a negotiated maximum if you prefer (we've done that before for POCs).

3) Cancellation/clawback: If BrightLabs signs a 12-month commit and then terminates within 30 days without cause, the outstanding portion of the launch credit is clawed back as an invoice charge. For pilot-only engagements (no post-pilot commit), launch credit is a one-time invoice credit and not recoverable — we treat pilot credits as marketing promo credits for evaluation. We can put the exact wording in the SOW (I can run legal language with Laura if needed).

Worked example (pilot -> Tier A commit):
- Pilot: 1,200,000 tokens used, list price = $0.60/1k -> invoice $720. Launch credit $12,000 offsets pilot fully (credits applied as invoice line item).
- Post-pilot commit: Tier A (12% discount) applied to subsequent months; first month after commit billed normally with discount; 25% of the credit released on first invoice after commit.

We can also do a conditional smaller up-front credit (e.g., $8k) if procurement prefers lower upfront risk. Karthik — any guardrails from RevOps on one-off credits?

If that all looks OK, Connor — let's schedule a 30-min commercial + procurement call tomorrow (4/13) to finalize the one-pager for legal. I can bring a simple SOW template.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
